newsitem.title: USA: Hilton Hotels raises ITT Corp. bid to $70 a share.
newsitem.headline: Hilton Hotels raises ITT Corp. bid to $70 a share.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp. said Wednesday it increased to $70 per share its hostile bid for ITT Corp. in a combination cash and stock transaction that would be worth approximately $8.3 billion.

Including the assumption of debt, the bid would be worth $11.5 billion. The new price represents a 64 percent premium over ITT's trading price prior to the original commencement of Hilton's offer of $55 per share, worth $6.5 billion, in January, Hilton said.
In a July efffort to thwart Hilton, ITT announced a creative restructuring plan to split the company into three pieces and buy back stock.

"Having had the opportunity to review ITT's partial tender offer and break-up plan, we believe our revised offer represents a full and attractive price for ITT shareholders and is vastly superior to the plan announced by ITT last month," said Hilton chief executive Stephen Bollenbach.
He said the transaction, designed to preserve Hilton's investment grade credit rating, is expected to be non-dilutive to Hilton's 1998 earnings and accretive thereafter.

Hilton said will be amending its cash tender for a majority of the shares of ITT to offer $70 per share. Following consummation of the tender offer, Hilton would then complete a second-step merger in which the remaining ITT shares would be converted into shares of Hilton common stock having a value of $70 per ITT share, subject to appropriate collar provisions.
